newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares fall prey to profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares fall prey to profit taking.

text.p: Slovenian shares reversed a five-day winning steak to fall 1.04 percent on Tuesday, driven down by profit taking after recent spectacular gains.
"Today's falling is no surprise and was caused by profit taking. I do not expect shares to fall much longer," Darko Gojcic, a trader at brokerage Veritas said.
The 10-share SBI index fell 13.56 points to 1,287.7.
The index had risen 11.76 percent the previous five days.
Turnover eased to 394.8 million tolars from 445.3 million tolars. Overall 15 shares fell and three rose, while another seven were untraded.
Drug producer Lek's A issue was the most active share, shedding 1.66 percent to 24,880 tolars on volume of 7,437 shares for total turnover of 185.8 million tolars.
"Lek remains one of the most interesting shares for foreign buyers," one trader said, expecting fresh buying.
Brokerage Dadas was the leading decliner, falling 11.93 percent to 6,420 tolars on volume of eight shares.
Preferred shares of bank Dolenjska banka were the biggest gainers surging 6.81 percent to 12,390 tolars on volume of 150 shares.
